justification.statement: stage_order is a topological sort: repeatedly placing the first listed row with no unplaced predecessor puts every orbit before every orbit its seed's collateral moves
justification.text: Each round places the first listed row whose predecessors are all placed and releases the rows its collateral moves (Kahn's algorithm), so a row comes before every row its collateral names. Rows on a cycle, and rows held behind one, are never released; the answer lists them in `cycle`.

evidence.label: LB2 stage order on listed rows, cycles included (LP3 test)

justification.text: The technical report's proposition, at the commit that last changed it: with the certified setup and frame coverage, the orientation corrections and an acyclic raw-seed collateral graph, solving every orbit before the orbits its seed's collateral moves keeps each completed orbit solved at later macro boundaries. The next raw seed fixes the completed orbits, since its collateral lies on later orbits, and every conjugate of it by a legal setup fixes them too. It holds at macro boundaries only (Net): during a macro, pieces of completed orbits can move and return.

reason.idea: Solve an orbit before the orbits its seed disturbs. Each later seed, and every setup's version of it, then leaves the finished orbits as they are at the end of each macro, although their pieces may move and come back during one.

by_hand.not_meant: A stage order is one order the collateral allows; it is not the only one and not a plan the program chooses for the solver. It keeps finished orbits in place at macro boundaries, not after every letter.

steps.check: Orbit 30 is in orbit 26's collateral, so 30 has one predecessor, 26.

Every row is placed: no cycle.
